description: Xanthos is a Python hydrological model developed at the Joint Global Change Research Institute for global water-availability analysis. Its documented standard configuration uses a half-degree grid and monthly time steps for historical or future climate forcing. Components calculate potential evapotranspiration, runoff and river routing, with calibration and hydropower modules added in version 2. Users select input files, parameters and outputs through a configuration file. Runoff, streamflow, accessible-water and hydropower estimates can inform water-supply and electricity-system scenarios. The repository and Python package are free under the Battelle licence labelled BSD 2-Clause, with an additional naming restriction. Xanthos complements GCAM by producing water-system information, but can also be used separately. A limitation is its coarse global resolution and dependence on forcing and calibration choices; modelled historical output is not itself an observation. Example data are obtained separately through a package helper. No input archive, hydrological simulation or calibration was run.
